questions.questionText: Aman starts walking towards North and covers 3 km. Then Aman turns right and walks 2 km, and finally turns right and walks 2 km. In which direction is Aman walking now?
questions.hint: Trace each turn sequentially from the standard compass rose (NESW).
questions.explanation: A right turn from North is East, and another right turn leads to South. Therefore, Aman is finally walking towards South.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Start facing North.
Step 2: First turn (turns right) sets the intermediate direction.
Step 3: Final turn (turns right) leads to facing South.
questions.memoryTip: Clockwise sequence of cardinal directions is always N -> E -> S -> W.

questions.questionText: Priya starts from point P and travels 3 km towards North, then turns right and travels 4 km to reach point Q. What is the shortest distance between points P and Q?

questions.explanation: Net North-South displacement = 30 m North - 24 m South = 6 m North. Net East-West displacement = 24 m East - 16 m West = 8 m East. Shortest distance = √(6² + 8²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 m. Since net coordinates are (+East, +North), the direction from X to Y is North-East.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Calculate vertical displacement: North - South = 30 - 24 = 6 m North.
Step 2: Calculate horizontal displacement: East - West = 24 - 16 = 8 m East.
Step 3: Distance = √(6² + 8²) = 10 m.
Step 4: Relative direction is North-East.
questions.memoryTip: Net displacement method: Group all North/South movements together and all East/West movements together.

questions.explanation: Net North-South displacement = 15 m North - 9 m South = 6 m North. Net East-West displacement = 20 m East - 12 m West = 8 m East. Shortest distance = √(6² + 8²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 m. Since net coordinates are (+East, +North), the direction from X to Y is North-East.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Calculate vertical displacement: North - South = 15 - 9 = 6 m North.
Step 2: Calculate horizontal displacement: East - West = 20 - 12 = 8 m East.
Step 3: Distance = √(6² + 8²) = 10 m.
Step 4: Relative direction is North-East.
questions.memoryTip: Net displacement method: Group all North/South movements together and all East/West movements together.

questions.explanation: Net North-South displacement = 25 m North - 19 m South = 6 m North. Net East-West displacement = 16 m East - 8 m West = 8 m East. Shortest distance = √(6² + 8²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 m. Since net coordinates are (+East, +North), the direction from X to Y is North-East.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Calculate vertical displacement: North - South = 25 - 19 = 6 m North.
Step 2: Calculate horizontal displacement: East - West = 16 - 8 = 8 m East.
Step 3: Distance = √(6² + 8²) = 10 m.
Step 4: Relative direction is North-East.
questions.memoryTip: Net displacement method: Group all North/South movements together and all East/West movements together.

questions.questionText: One morning after sunrise, Aman and Rohit were standing in a garden facing each other. If the shadow of Rohit fell exactly to the left of Aman, which direction was Aman facing?
questions.hint: In the morning, the Sun is in the East, so all shadows point towards the West.

Step 2: The shadow falls to the right of Deepak -> Deepak's right is West.
Step 3: A person whose right is West must be facing South.
questions.memoryTip: Sunrise Rule: Facing North -> Shadow is on Left. Facing South -> Shadow is on Right.

questions.hint: In the evening, the Sun is in the West, so all shadows point towards the East. Pay attention to who is asked!
questions.explanation: In the evening, the Sun is in the West, so shadows fall towards the East. Since Sanjay's shadow is to Sanjay's left, Sanjay's left is East, which means Sanjay is facing South. Because Sanjay and Tanvi are facing each other, Tanvi must be facing the opposite direction, which is North.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Time is evening -> Sun is West -> All shadows fall East.
Step 2: Sanjay's shadow falls to Sanjay's left -> Sanjay's left is East.
Step 3: For left to be East, Sanjay must face South.
Step 4: Since Tanvi faces Sanjay, Tanvi faces North.
questions.memoryTip: Sunset Rule: Facing North -> Shadow is on Right. Facing South -> Shadow is on Left.

questions.questionText: One morning, Divya was performing yoga with head down and feet up facing North. In which direction will Divya's right hand point?

questions.questionText: At 12:00 noon on a sunny day in June, in which direction does a vertical flagpole cast its shadow?
options: No shadow / negligible right under base
questions.hint: At solar noon, the Sun is directly overhead at zenith.
questions.explanation: At exactly 12:00 noon, the Sun is directly overhead (zenith) in the sky. Therefore, vertical objects cast virtually no lateral shadow or the shadow falls directly underneath the base.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Solar position at 12 noon is directly overhead.
Step 2: Rays strike vertically downwards.
Step 3: No lateral shadow is cast in any cardinal direction.
questions.memoryTip: At 12 noon, shadows have zero length horizontally because the sun is directly overhead.
